title: What Happens When You Get Hangry?
description:
Send this to the friend who gets mean before lunch.
In a 21-day study of 64 adults, hunger tracked 37% of the ups and downs in irritability and 34% in anger (Swami et al., PLOS ONE 2022). When you go a while without eating, blood sugar drops, stress hormones like cortisol and adrenaline kick in, and impulse control can slip (Cleveland Clinic). Twist: in US experiments, hunger only made ambiguous symbols look worse after a negative photo, and hungry people who tuned into their feelings didn't turn hangry (MacCormack & Lindquist, Emotion 2018). Often shaky, sweaty or confused and you don't have diabetes? The NHS says see a doctor.
Next Body File: why a tiny paper cut hurts so much (your fingertips are packed with nerves).
Follow Body Files for a new one every day.

Re-hook: hard cut to a white lab room (new scene) where a hungry hero sees two photo cards (storm cloud vs plain chair) and then the same random squiggle symbol; after the storm card his thumbs-down appears, after the chair card nothing changes, and pill B gets the check. safety: Curious-friend tone, no personal medical advice. 37% is voiced as 'tracked' (variance explained, not cause); hormone surge and impulse-control claims follow Cleveland Clinic wording. NHS low-blood-sugar 'see a doctor' pointer is in the description (not voiced, to keep the answer after 70%). No dieting, calorie or weight talk. Schematic visuals only; the snap at the coworker is a short huff, no aggression shown.

engagement.guess: A everything vs B only bad moments (answer: B, only bad moments; MacCormack & Lindquist 2018 Emotion: hungrier people rated ambiguous pictographs as more negative only after a negative image; neutral or positive images had no effect. Option A is the common belief that hunger makes everything annoying)
